From Prototype to Market: A Hands-on Workshop for Hardware Founders 

What does it really take to move from a working prototype to a market-ready product?
Recently we hosted an event in Coimbatore as a part of Velocity - Kotak BizLabs Accelerator Programme, a CSR initiative by Kotak Mahindra Bank in partnership with NSRCEL, where hardware founders explored the journey beyond building the technology and learnt why customer validation must come before product development.

The session covered the following key lessons:
👉 Start with the problem, not the technology - Validate a real customer need before building
👉 Understand the customer - Identify the user, buyer, pain point, alternatives, and urgency
👉 Focus on customer discovery - Ask open-ended questions and listen before pitching
👉 Validate before you build - Test assumptions with real customers through experiments and MVPs
👉 Prototype ≠ Product - Build for reliability, repeatability, cost, serviceability, and scalability
👉 Anticipate hardware risks - Consider supply chains, components, connectivity, regulations, and certifications early
👉 Build vs Buy - Focus on your core USP and partner for non-core capabilities
👉 Adopt the right founder mindset -  Stay open to feedback, be willing to pivot, and keep iterating

The path from prototype to market isn't just about making the technology work. It's about proving that it solves a real problem, for the right customer, in a way they are willing to pay for.

Sustain Plus | mach33

Up to 15% of food produced in India perishes due to lack of refrigeration. Medicines and vaccines also depend on consistent cooling from storage to delivery. Yet refrigeration remains unaffordable to many farmers and traders due to high upfront costs. Reefer trucks running on fossil fuels add to the ecological cost of this operation as well. Currently, there exists a gap of 3.2+ million metric tonne in India’s cold-chain capacity. 

Tan90 Thermal, one of the winners of Social Alpha’s Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy (Edition 3), has developed a low-cost, proprietary Phase Change Material-based portable cold storage solution, offered as cooling-as-a-service, to make farm-to-fork transportation more efficient and less carbon-intensive. 
Tan90 Thermal is an example of how hands-on mentorship, product development assistance, and catalytic funding can reimagine innovation in energy access and efficiency, especially in critical sectors like food and pharma. 

If your innovation can make a real impact on energy access, efficiency, storage, or the transition to renewables, apply to Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy.

From rooftops, basements, and warehouses to hydroponics, aeroponics, and controlled environment agriculture, urban farming is often presented as the future of food. But is it truly a scalable solution, or sometimes just a sustainability theatre?
